title: Customer compatibility matrix, pin-exemptions, and gated shadow trials for model onboarding
creator: Marco Ruiz
description:
Problem: Enterprise customers frequently request exceptions to model version pinning or earlier access to new model variants, but current intake and gating process is binary (approve/deny) and lacks a compatibility-first decision path. This leads to delays, uncoordinated rollouts, and unexpected regressions for large customers.

Goal: Design and implement a customer-driven compatibility matrix that captures customer workloads, acceptance criteria, and required compatibility tests; define a formal 'pin-exemption' workflow for time-bound exceptions; and build a gated shadow trial flow that lets customers run new model versions in a constrained shadow environment tied to evals and safety checks. The outcome should reduce manual back-and-forth, decrease approval time for gated trials, and give engineering and PM more observable signals for safe pining/deprecations.
background: We onboard ~3–5 enterprise model requests per week that ask for: (1) early access to bleeding-edge model variants, (2) temporary pin exemptions allowing traffic to hit a new version, or (3) a delayed deprecation. Current playbooks (see PM-5387, PM-6420) cover admission scoring but do not encode workload compatibility matrices or a formal short-term exemption lifecycle. Platform and runtime teams have expressed concerns about regressions and unknown performance tradeoffs when exceptions are granted without structured trials.
proposal:
1) Introduce a compact compatibility matrix template capturing: workload type (chat/generation/embedding/rerank), typical token lengths, latency SLOs, non-functional constraints (quantization, on-prem), and golden prompts for regression checks.
2) Add a 'pin-exemption' ticket type: timeboxed (max 30 days), with required preflight checks and a rollback plan. Pin-exemptions must include explicit acceptance criteria and an auto-expire behavior.
3) Implement a gated shadow trial feature in the catalog: customers can run a percentage of traffic or a shadow copy of requests against the candidate model. Shadow trials are paired with an automated eval harness that runs the compatibility matrix (functional + quality + perf).
4) Define approval matrix that ties customer tier + risk signals + eval pass/fail to one of 4 actions: white-list (auto-approve), require canary, require shadow trial, deny.
5) Surface results and a single CTA in the Console to request/approve/monitor pin-exemption and shadow trials (links to logs, eval diffs, and rollback actions).
acceptance_criteria:
- Compatibility matrix template available in Confluence and as a catalog intake field.
- New pin-exemption ticket type in Linear with required fields enforced by intake form.
- Shadow trial prototype deployed to staging that can run 1% traffic and capture token-level diffs.
- Automated eval harness runs at least 3 regression checks (latency, hallucination metric, correctness on golden prompts) and reports pass/fail.
- Approval matrix documented and validated with Security and Compliance.
- Metrics: average approval time for enterprise model requests reduced from 9 days to <=4 days in pilot customers.
rollout_plan:
Phase 1 (2 weeks): finalize compatibility matrix template and intake form; run 3 pilot intake requests with account managers.
Phase 2 (4 weeks): implement pin-exemption ticket type and gating rules; build minimal UI for requesting exemption in Console (request form + links).
Phase 3 (6 weeks): deploy shadow-trial in staging and run pilot with two enterprise customers; integrate automated eval harness.
Phase 4 (post-pilot): iterate, codify runbooks, and enable for general availability on catalog-2025.03.
Rollback: pin-exemptions auto-expire; shadow trials default to no-write and cannot alter customer production state until explicitly promoted.
risks:
- Shadow trials may not surface subtle data-dependent regressions if test set is too small.
- Allowing pin-exemptions increases operational overhead for runtime engineers.
- Compliance or legal constraints on some customers may disallow even shadow traffic in shared environments.
- UI complexity could slow requests if not designed for quick consumption.
open_questions: What are the exact golden prompt templates per workload?
Should pin-exemptions be allowed for on-prem/private only?
How do we surface an easy rollback for customers with private deployments?
